en: The Recorded Sayings of Master Wuchu.
Compiled by his disciples De Pu and others from the Recorded Sayings of Master Wuchu while he resided at Faxiang Chan Monastery in the Prefecture of Lin’an.
In the seventh month of the first year of the Chunyou era, the Master entered the monastery.
Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "To level what is high by descending into it is difficult for anyone to accomplish. I, the new Dharma-teacher, shall open a separate path for all of you.
He then ascended the seat and held up the incense, saying: "This single offering of incense is respectfully presented to extend our prayers for [the Emperor’s] longevity."
May His Majesty the Emperor enjoy ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years of longevity.

We respectfully pray that he may govern with the Golden Wheel, such that the ten Flower-Treasury Seas shall all come under his dominion; and that the Jade Calendar may ever be renewed, as the five Sumeru Mountains stand tall, surpassing the peaks of long life.

[Next, holding the incense, he says: We offer this incense on behalf of the Grand Councilor, the Pacification Commissioner, the Acting Governor, together with all the meritorious nobles of the entire prefecture.
May your years and blessings increase. Again, holding up the incense, he said:

"This incense is burned within the burner, offered on behalf of the Great Master Beijian, currently abiding at Jingci Guangxiao Chan Temple, to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk. He takes his seat. (The questions and answers are not recorded. Then he says:
"Dancing with the Tai’a sword, the empty wheel leaves no trace; performing the music of Xuanyuan, one does not abide by old conventions."
For the family of patch-robed monks, the mind does not dwell on the profound, and the eyes do not hang upon the door.

Whether emerging or entering, whether fully or partially upholding [the Dharma], these are still merely playing with the rules and standards. But what is the single phrase that transcends the school? [He strikes the whisk and says:
"When the wutong trees are high, the phoenixes and peacocks perch; when the sea is vast, the dragons and serpents swirl. Again, he cites Nanquan’s address to the assembly, saying: "Wen..."
"Last night at the third watch, Shu and Puxian got up and started fighting. I gave each of them twenty blows and chased them out.
Zhaozhou came forward and asked, "Whom did the Master intend for the blows to fall upon? Nanquan said, "What fault has Old Teacher Wang committed?"

Zhaozhou performed his prostrations, and Nanquan immediately returned to the abbot’s quarters. The Master said, "The wind arises from the grass; playing with cleverness results in folly—this is not lacking in Nanquan and Zhaozhou.
Is there anyone here now who will exert themselves for the sake of the assembly?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Real does not stand; the false is fundamentally empty. Seven hollows and eight protrusions; four openings and six penetrations.
The sound of pines mingling with rain—the mountains are long still; spring colors linger with the cold, yet the flowers are naturally red."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: Once, while Qifu and Layman Pang were traveling together, the Layman took a step forward and said, "I am one step stronger than you, Master.
Qifu replied, "There is no front or back; you old man want to be first. The Layman said, "The bitterness within bitterness is not yet this one phrase.
Qifu said, "I fear you will not be satisfied, old man. The Layman said, "If you are not satisfied, Qifu is capable [of it]."
"What are you doing? Feng said, "If I had a staff in my hand, I would strike without weariness. The Master then gave him a slap with his palm and said, "Not very good.
Only then did Feng pick up his staff, but he was seized by the Master, who said, "You thief! Today you have suffered a total defeat."
Feng laughed and said, "This is my clumsiness; this is your cleverness. The scholar then clapped his hands and said, "An equal match! An equal match!
The Master said, "These two old men do not let even a hair’s breadth of difference pass them by, yet they remain unaware of where their own seams have gaped.
It would be well to tie them together into a single bundle and cast them into the Yangtze River."
The Record of the Chan Master at Xianci Chan Monastery in Anji Prefecture, compiled and edited by his disciples De Pu and others.
According to the Abbot’s quarters, [the Master] held up his staff and said: "Vertical and horizontal, encompassing all; when it comes to practicing benevolence, do not yield. As for you all, what..."
He did not attempt to grasp it directly. Holding up his staff, he said, "What a pity!
He ascended the seat;

after the ritual for the Emperor was completed (the questions and answers are not recorded), he said: "Those who clearly know that there is something cannot speak of it; it is like salt falling into the soy sauce."
Though one speaks clearly of what can be attained, one does not know that it exists. It is like biting into the sweet head of sugarcane.

Whether one speaks of what can be attained or what cannot, whether one knows its existence or does not—this is the jackal howling while the lion roars. Let us set this aside for now; consider instead these words:

"The Buddhas did not appear in the world; the Patriarchs did not come from the West. The Buddha-dharma pervades the world, yet those who discuss the profound do not open their mouths. This is but a heap of refuse.
From antiquity to the present, people have exhausted their every effort, yet they have failed to sweep it clean.

This mountain monk, for his part, has but short sleeves to grace this banquet and possesses no exquisite dance. Suppose, however, there were a man who came forth, overturned the meditation seat, and shouted the assembly into dispersal—what then?
(He strikes the whisk. "The Yellow River clears itself but once every three thousand years."
Again, Master Shilou was approached by a monk who came for an audience. After bowing, the monk rose and said, "I do not yet recognize my original nature;
I pray that the Master will provide a skillful means to point it out. Shilou said, "Shilou has no ears. The monk said, "I myself know that I am at fault. Shilou said, [Silence].
"The old monk also has a fault. The monk asked, "Where does the Master’s fault lie? Lou said, "The fault lies in your being in the wrong place.
The monk bowed, and Lou struck him. The Master said, "Burying one's head to complain; the balance and mirror are impartial.
To join a broken string with *lin* glue requires a truly skilled hand."
On account of the rain, the Master ascended the hall. He cited the case where Jingqing asked a monk, "What is that sound outside the gate?
The monk said, "The sound of raindrops falling on the eaves. Jingqing said, "Sentient beings are inverted; they lose themselves and pursue external things.
The monk said, "I am exactly like this; what about you, Master? Jingqing said, "I have not lost myself. The monk asked, "As for 'not having lost oneself,' what is the meaning of this?"
Qingyun said: "Leaving one's body may still be easy; shedding the entire self to realize the Way must be difficult. The Master composed a verse: "Drop by drop before the eaves, heard or not heard?
Jingqing has no tongue—whom can he discuss it with? Through the night, several bouts of heavy rain have poured down; It overwhelms the setting sun, its green reaching to the very roots."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Empty-handed, grasping a hoe; a man’s life fears Rāhu. Walking, yet riding a water buffalo; a stone tiger gives birth to a fleshly panther.
A person passes over a bridge; the bridge flows, but the water does not flow. Xiyang (the Sun God) whips the white sun; Shaohao (the Autumn God) conducts the clear autumn.
Master Fu’s throat has been pinched once by Xianci, and it is firmly secured. Is there anyone who can turn their body around?"
"Is it the one who exhales? He let out a shout and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you seek it, you will not find it; if you do not seek it, how can it be manifested? Strike the blind spot at the crown of the head! It is brilliant and resplendent.
After the rain falls upon the mulberry fields, the silk-like soil is smooth and rich; when the wind comes across the wheat ridges, the aroma of cakes and pastries wafts forth."
Ascending the hall, he said: "I only wish that you would empty all that exists; be careful not to fill what does not exist.
To turn one's fur robe inside out, to eat sugarcane upside down—Pang Jushi overturns his strainer and haggles for the sky at the crossroads.
Is there anyone here who can truly accept and practice this? He gave a shout.
Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Imperial Birthday, he held up his staff and said: "Lofty and unsurpassed; venerable and peerless. It encompasses the ten voids and inspires all existence.
Let the nectar descend, let the sweet springs flow, let the *zhicao* grasses grow, and let the phoenixes and qilin arrive.

If one were to proceed in this manner, even the reigns of the sovereigns Yao and Shun would still have their transformative influence remaining. "If it is not like this at all," he struck the staff and said: "The five winds."
For ten years, the harvests have been perennially bountiful. In the wilds, one occasionally hears the songs of those who strike the *rang* blocks.

[The Master] ascends the hall and cites Dongshan’s address to the assembly, saying: "Before Bodhidharma came, winter was cold and summer was hot; after Bodhidharma came, the night was dark and the day was bright.
If you people can utter a single word of plain reality, it will be like tasting salt and knowing its saltiness. [He] eats... [and so on].

When vinegar is smelled, its sourness is perceived. If you cannot bring it down [to a definitive conclusion], it will remain at the threshold of Kāśyapa’s gate. The Master said: "The Fifth Patriarch, our venerable teacher, has already added a handle to his almsbowl.
I, however, am not like this. Before Bodhidharma had come, there were earthen drums beaten with clappers made of bundled grass;

after Bodhidharma came, there was the shadow of a bow mistaken for a snake in a cup. If you can bring down a single turn of plain, practical speech, you will have no share of receiving a blow of the staff. If you cannot..."
It is not permitted; nor does he yet have the lot to receive a blow of the staff. Since Xianci calls himself a descendant of Dongshan, why is he so diametrically opposed?
Amidst the fragrance of the lotus, summer is driven away; within the shadows of the wutong tree, autumn is ushered in.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Master Dazi (Striking the Ground). Whenever a student would come to inquire, he would simply strike the ground once.
One day, a monk asked his attendant, "The Master always strikes the ground once whenever someone asks him a question; what is the meaning of this?
The attendant took a piece of firewood from under the hearth and threw it into the cauldron. The Master said, "Xianci wanted to ask."
"Everyone, if you say there is an indication, why did he only strike the ground? If you say there is no indication, why did he nevertheless strike the ground?
When the disciple acted thus, was it a case of adapting according to the inner meaning, or was there some other principle at work?
Even if one were to understand immediately upon hearing this, how could that suffice?"

Ascending the hall on the Double Ninth: Fallen leaves scatter; singing crickets chirp incessantly. The chrysanthemums by the fence flash with golden blossoms; the moon branches shed golden dust. "Three threes make nine"—there is a paradox here;
"two nines make eighteen"—there is no peer to this. If you can understand it thus, [you have grasped it].
In the autumn sky, the skeletal bones of the mountains are exposed. If you do not understand this, when the waters recede, the stones emerge.
On the first day of winter, ascending to the hall: before the peak of Shaoshi, the ice withers and the snow ages; atop Mount Dayu, the sun scorches and the wind blows.
How many heroic spirits have been buried alive? Their poison spreads unchecked. Here, among us monks, we employ the strategy of "unseating the horse to shoot the barbarian.
Let them be seventy-three or eighty-four years old; yin reaches its extreme at the hour of Hai, and yang begins to arise at the hour of Zi.
Nevertheless, this staff of manifest compassion will not let them off. Why? Because the Yellow River has nine bends.
Recorded Sayings from Xiangtian Xingjiao Chan Monastery in Shaoxing Prefecture.
At the Buddha Hall: "The past has already passed; the future is yet to come. As for the present—how about that? [He spreads his sitting cloth and says: "Buddha!"
The prophecy at Vulture Peak has been utterly ruined.
Ascending the seat, he offered prayers for the Emperor;
the questions and answers are not recorded. He then said: "There is a path before the pivot of the mind; do not speak of elephants tilling and birds weeding. Beyond the norm..."
Clarify the essential point. What does it matter if the wind blows and the thunder roars? Just so, just so.

Whether it be the Buddha-dhyāna or the Patriarch-dhyāna—leave these instruments of war from the era of Great Peace to one side. You people, throughout the six periods of the day and night, when walking, simply walk; when sitting, simply sit.
In total, you must not move even a single hair’s breadth. Why? Because "a thousand peaks look toward Mount Hua; ten thousand streams flow solemnly into the vast ocean.
Again, he raised an instance: When Master Zhuyu was standing with the assembly, he said, "Just standing here in silence like this, there is no place for speech—a truly stifling situation.
A monk prepared to step forward and ask a question, but Zhuyu said, "Exerting one's utmost strength for the sake of the community," and then returned to his quarters.
The Master held up [the whisk] and said: "This one stroke beneath the *zhuyou* (Euonymus) tree is enough to startle the multitude; yet, alas, there is still no path for emerging from it.
Nevertheless, with every cause and every event, wisdom does not fail to grow."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Open the mouth and you lose; close the mouth and you perish. Stripped bare and revealed in purity, the arrow is already upon the string.
Do you all see Xiangtian? After a long silence, he said: "The eyelashes and eyebrows have all fallen away; one knows not on what day they shall grow back again."
Ascending the hall on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month: Stone people whisper to one another; plum blossoms open in the cold valley as spring arrives.
Snowdrops fall like rain from the clear eaves. How perfectly clear! What is there to see? Nanquan does not beat the drum of Yanguan.
Ascending the hall on the occasion of the National Foundation Day: Without shifting from his fundamental station, auspicious responses manifest among humanity.

Surpassing all spirits, he emerges as the foremost; within the tip of a single hair, he encompasses the great chiliocosm. The myriad species flourish in joy, like the delight of a spring terrace; the ten thousand realms submit in peace, like the security of a bedrock foundation.
Let them wear the sky and tread the earth, pounding the soil and drumming their bellies, unaware of the vastness of heaven and earth.
Furthermore, how does a patch-robed monk beneath the forest trees offer prayers for the Emperor?
Holding upside-down a single holeless flute, he carelessly blows it through to the fullness of ten-thousand-year joy.
[He] ascends the hall and says: "If one speaks of the body of names, the body of phrases, or the body of sentences—whether they are this or that—a Zen practitioner is like oil mixed with flour."
"A fly sees blood. Today, everything has been laid out in full. [He strikes the whisk. "The seawater is salty;
the river water is fresh. He ascends the hall and says: He cites the attendant Kuò asking Dégù, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? Dégù replied:
"What? What? Shan said. Kuò replied, "The imperial decree summons the flying dragon horse; a lame turtle sticks its head out. Shan then desisted.
The next day, they met at the bathhouse. Shan patted Kuò on the back and said, "Regarding yesterday's case, what was it like?
Kuò said, "Old man, only today have you finally woken up. Shan again desisted. The Master said, "Attendant Kuò..."

One sees the sharpness of the awl’s point, but one does not see the squareness of the chisel’s head. Do you all wish to recognize Deshan? The thief is right there in human form. Entering the hall, he said:
"If no one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, though one possesses wisdom, one cannot realize it. The old barbarian has three hundred and sixty joints of bone."
The eighty-four thousand pores—when casually flayed open, they cannot avoid being encircled by layers upon layers. (He strikes the whisk.
Red blossoms in the third month of spring; white clouds over a thousand peaks at dawn.
The Discourse Record of Zhimen Chan Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture, compiled and edited by the disciples De Pu and others, based on the Abbot’s quarters.
Holding his staff horizontally across his chest, he said: "In my place here, I do not stir a single mechanism, nor do I shift a single realm. You..."
"Where do equals meet? [Dongshan] leaned on his staff and said, "It is upon the mouth.
[The Master ascended] the Dharma seat and said, "This seat is high and vast; I cannot ascend it. [Dongshan] said, "Tsk! What kind of talk is this?
"But where there is a path to ascend, even higher than that, people will walk."
Ascending the seat, after the verses for the Emperor have been recited, he says: "Movement is without stopping; the Yellow River is thoroughly turbid from root to bottom.
Stillness is without movement; the bright sun shines in the midst of the sky. Thus it may be so, and not thus it may also be; both 'thus' and 'not thus' are entirely acceptable. Yesterday...
Elder Rixiangtian was the Master of White Rock this morning. Ceasing cultivation and resting from sowing, he reduced the hearths while adding to the ranks.
Since it is thus that fixed karma cannot be escaped, how could one merely follow the beaten path and tread the old tracks? Even so, what exactly has been accomplished in the end?
A single breath speaks not, yet it contains all forms; where do the myriad spirits offer thanks for this impartiality?
Again, it is cited: A monk once asked Zhaozhou, "When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it? Zhaozhou said, "I, this old monk, simply watch.
Commentary: The old man Zhaozhou only knows how to steer against the wind; he is unable to set his sails with the current.
An old acquaintance visits; ascending the hall, when masters meet, one goes west and one goes east. A broken stele is inscribed with white characters;
pine trees are planted by the road. The size of Zhimen’s cauldron and the length of its ladle handle have all been scrutinized through by everyone.
Nevertheless, thirty years hence, Grandfather Lü will cast his line.
Ascending the hall to pray for rain: "If there is even a hair’s breadth of separation, every sound and word is entirely the Buddha’s teaching;

yet when beyond the reach of the spiritual capacity [of the listener], there is not a single deviation. The entire Tripitaka is entirely the Mara’s teaching. When the fan leaps and bounds up to the Thirty-three Heavens, it strikes the nostrils of Śakra;
when the carp of the Eastern Sea is struck with a single blow, the rain pours down like an overturned basin. But what about this?
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know that it exists; once water is spilled, it is hard to retrieve. The cat and the white ox, however, do know that it exists;
this is like adding a head atop one's own head. The sun sets in the west by day; the Yellow River flows north.
Pushing over the mountain at the gate, let them sit upon the ground and watch Yangzhou."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: When the World-Honored One ascended the seat and sat in silence, Ānanda struck the gavel and said, "We pray that the World-Honored One will preach the Dharma.
The World-Honored One said, "In this assembly there are two bhikṣus who have violated the Vinaya; for this reason, I do not preach the Dharma.
Ānanda, using his supernormal power of reading others' minds, observed these bhikṣus and subsequently expelled them. The World-Honored One remained silent once more. Ānanda again...
Baoyun said: "The two bhikṣus have already been expelled; why does the World-Honored One not preach the Dharma? The World-Honored One replied:
"I have vowed never to preach the Dharma for those of the Two Vehicles. Baoyun remarked: "At that time, Ānanda should have simply remained silent toward the World-Honored One."
Say this: "How regrettable! So that you may avoid being called a person of the Two Vehicles.
Entering the hall, he held his staff to probe the water, surely knowing its depth; once the balance scale was suspended, he surely examined the weight.
For the patch-robed monks, leaving one forest and entering another community, horns grow upon their eyes and needles are contained within their bags. (He took up the whisk.)
He drew a single line and said: "The heavy gates were once fully opened; yet, though we walk hand in hand, we do not return together. Ascending the hall, he raised the following case:
"When Fuyan was in the assembly of his late teacher at Dongshan, he served as a lay practitioner (*huashishi*) for the Wuweijun army.

While on the road, he suffered a fall and attained realization. Upon returning, he recounted this experience. Later, the Master appointed him as the guest prefect (*zhike*). There, while tending the fire, he attained a sudden, profound awakening. Nevertheless—"
Every time he entered the room for instruction, he was unable to attain profound realization. He asked for further guidance with composure, to which Dongshan replied, "I have a parable for you:
it is like a person leading an ox through a window lattice. The two horns and four hooves all pass through at once, yet only the tail cannot get through.
He then offered this verse: Once entered Xianyang, all former travels end; Spring winds blow through terraces and pavilions facing fragrant islets.
"It is not that the fine scenery lingers to intoxicate people; it is simply that the traveler’s intoxication does not cease.
On the day of concluding the summer retreat, he ascended the hall, took up his staff, and said: "Today marks the end of the summer.

Whatever was realized or learned within these ninety days—whether it be the path of mystery or the path of doctrine—I cast it away into other worlds. Yet even this mountain monk cannot avoid [the consequences]."
He hosted a family banquet to reward their labor. Holding up his staff, he said: "I urge you to drink one more cup;
once you have passed the Yang Pass to the west, there will be no old friends left."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: A monk asked Jinfeng, "A function that does not fall into the categories of sage or ordinary—please, Master, speak of it apart from these. Jinfeng said, "Jinfeng’s eyes are no small thing. The monk said, "In that case, with one stroke on the lute, the sovereign is immediately cleared. Jinfeng said: [The Master] ascended the hall. He cited the case:

A monk asked Jinfeng, "Regarding the function that does not fall into the categories of sage or ordinary, please, Master, speak of it apart from these. Jinfeng said, "Jinfeng’s eyes are no small thing. The monk said, "If so, then with one stroke on the lute, the sovereign is immediately cleared. Jinfeng said:
"Another way—how could one possibly compete with that? The monk said, "What about the words spoken for the sake of sentient beings? Fēng said, "The Sovereign of Sudden Purity.
The monk said, "If it were not for Jīnfēng, it would indeed be difficult. Fēng said, "A man of fine strategy; even Zhōu Kē would have to yield his seat."
The monk said, "If you do not accept these words, I fear you will fall into delusion. Feng said, "Accept what words? The monk said, "Why trouble yourself to bring them up again?
Feng said, "A mute man chasing a boat; there is no lack of stubbornness and stupidity here. The Master said, "Red beard, beard red."
A snake swallows a jar; the jar swallows the snake. When one examines this closely, neither is fully resolved.
At that time, it was truly difficult even for Jin-feng not to be wrong when he saw this. He said to him, "The Master shall have no place to stay elsewhere.
This not only cuts off the entanglements, but also leaves this monk with no way to hide his body. Let those with eyes discern this for themselves.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Language and activity have no connection [to the truth]. The bowl is coarse; the steamed rice is fine. Even non-language and non-activity have no connection.
The Master’s Peak is high; the Table Mountain is low. How do we see this? The deer steps into the mossy crags with ease;
the white phoenix flies from the sea-trees at leisure."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case where Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying: "At Wushan Ridge, I have already met you.
At Wangzhou Pavilion, I have already met you. Before the Sangha Hall, I have already met you. Later, Baofu asked Ehu:
"Setting aside for a moment the matter of the Sangha Hall, at what place do you meet me at Wushan Ridge and Wangzhou Pavilion? Ehu—
He hurried back to the abbot’s quarters, and Baofu immediately entered the monks’ hall. The Master composed a verse, saying: Three folds of autumn wind, the ancient melody is clear;
Shifting the *shang* and changing the *zheng*, to whom may it be heard? When Zhou Lang cast a glance, he spurred his whip and rode away; Beyond the clouds, several peaks stand green upon the river.
Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Imperial Birthday, [the Master] cited Caoshan’s instruction to the assembly:

“The vast and mysterious Great Way, the unattached True Teaching—this single rank has been extolled by the former masters of antiquity as the most wondrous and profound. One must examine it with care and discern it clearly:

the Sovereign represents the position of correctness; the Minister represents the position of partiality. When the Minister faces the Sovereign, it is ‘correctness within partiality’; when the Sovereign looks upon the Minister, it is ‘partiality within correctness.’”
"The way of sovereign and subject is in harmony" is a phrase that encompasses both aspects. The Master’s verse says: The sun strikes the golden plaque at the Gate of Heaven;

In the palace, the clear air perfumes the crimson feathered banners. The four seas and nine provinces all present their tribute; The spring breeze has arrived once more at the Ten-Thousand-Year Branch.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The World-Honored One spoke what is not spoken; in the first month of spring, it is still cold. Kāśyapa heard what is not heard;
in the second month of spring, it gradually warms. If you can understand this here, you will possess only the skill of the blind turtle.
He suddenly took up his staff, drew a line, and said: "The clouds over Xiangtan have vanished and the mountains emerge; the snow in the Ba Gorges has melted and the spring waters arrive."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this topic: "The World-Honored One, together with the assembly of sages, went to the Sixth Heaven to preach the Mahāsannipāta Sūtra.
He commanded all the fierce and malevolent ghosts and spirits from other lands and this world, from the human realm and the heavens above, to assemble entirely and receive the Buddha’s entrustment."
To protect the True Dharma: should there be any who do not attend, the Four Heavenly Kings shall fly fiery iron wheels after them to compel their assembly.
Once they have assembled, there shall be none who do not comply with the Buddha’s command; each shall make a great vow to protect the True Dharma.

There was only one Māra King who said to the World-Honored One: "Gautama, I shall wait until all sentient beings have attained Buddhahood, until the realm of sentient beings is empty and the very name 'sentient being' no longer exists; only then will I resolve to attain Bodhicitta. Tianyi said:
"To remain unchanging in the face of peril—this is truly a Great Man. "Virtuous ones," [the Master asked], "how would you apply a turning word for this? For Huang...
This is merely Laozi letting out his breath. Ordinarily, one’s supernatural powers, wondrous functions, wisdom, and eloquence are of no use at all.
Throughout the entire land of Jambudvīpa, there is no one who does not love the Buddha. Yet, when one arrives here, what is the Buddha and what is Māra? How can they be distinguished?
If you wish to recognize Māra, it is seeing light with eyes open; if you wish to recognize the Buddha, it is seeing darkness with eyes closed. Māra!
[The Master] said, "With this staff, I have at once pierced through the nostrils of both you and the Buddha. Miaoxi said, "I nearly mistook you for a demon king.
The Master said, "It is so; it is so. One may be brave when facing a great enemy, yet one still cannot escape the net of the Yellow-Faced Old Man.
It has brought trouble upon Tianyi Miaoxi, who has exhausted himself in his attempts to explain it away."
Ascending the hall upon leaving the hospital: Holding up a broken chopstick upside down, he stirs the vast blue sea; countless fish and dragons are startled in the dark.
With a single laugh, the mechanism is lightly turned; at midnight, the moonlight over East Lake shines bright.
The Recorded Sayings of the Chan Master of Daci Mingshan Jiaozhong Baoguo Chan Temple in Qingyuan Prefecture, compiled and edited by his disciples De Pu and others.
The Three Gates: The vast and great gateway is already perfected wherever one encounters it;
yet if you attempt to grasp even a single hair’s breadth of it, there is a ten-thousand-fathom iron mountain before you. All of you— [End of Text]
"Do you still believe this? He gives a shout.
At the Abbot’s quarters, he takes up his staff and says, "If I were to lift it up, you would immediately construct intellectual interpretations regarding the time before it was lifted.
If I do not lift it up, you would immediately attempt to exercise mastery over the place where it is not lifted. He leans on the staff and says, "The sword has long since been lost."
He ascended the seat.

Having finished offering incense and making prayers for the Emperor, he took his place and said: "Before a single edge is revealed, it is like emptiness containing emptiness; as soon as meaning and phrase manifest, it is like water entering water.
Is there anyone here who is in accord? At that time, a monk came forward and asked: "The golden cock crows at dawn; the jade phoenix..."
"Carrying flowers in its mouth. At this very moment, please offer a prayer for the Emperor on behalf of the Master. The Master said: "Striking the golden bell atop Mount Zhurong. The student asked:
"If that is so, then 'One breath remains silent, yet contains all forms; where can the myriad spirits go to thank the Impartial One? " The Master said:
"A red banner embroidered upon a ball of a hundred flowers. The student asked: "I recall Zhaozhou visiting Daci, and finding him sweeping the ground."
Next, Zhaozhou asked, "What is the essence of Prajñā? Daci replied, "What is the essence of Prajñā?
The Master said, "A pair of solitary wild geese fly high, striking the earth.
[The student] asked, "On the following day, while Zhaozhou was sweeping the ground, Daci asked again, 'What is the essence of Prajñā? Zhaozhou dropped his broom and laughed."
[The Master] laughed loudly. [The monk] asked, "And how about this? The Master said, "Two mandarin ducks standing alone by the pond.

The Master drew a circle and said respectfully, "Is it only this? Or is there something else? The junior monk drew a line through the circle and then prostrated.
The Master said, "A fierce tiger does not eat meat that has already been submitted."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following passage: "At the time of eating, the World-Honored One put on his robes, took up his bowl, and entered the great city of Śrāvastī to beg for food.

Having completed his alms-round through the city in proper sequence, he returned to his original location. When he had finished his meal, he put away his robes and bowl, washed his feet, arranged his seat, and sat down.
Subhūti said, "How rare, World-Honored One! The Master remarked, "Śākyamuni Old Man was three parts flat and two parts level."
Full. Suddenly pressed by Śūnyatā-janman (Huineng), he was unconsciously left with his wall collapsed and leaning against the support.
He ascended the hall (to thank the Supervisor of Receipts, and also to thank for the stele inscription for the Pagoda of Brother Bótíng).
"What does Heaven say? The four seasons proceed. What does Earth say? The myriad things are born. What does the patch-robed monk say? One day, the alms-bowl..."
"Crossing the dampness. He laughed and said, "The four mountains are green and then yellow. This is certainly so; yet, to have a turning phrase inscribed upon a stele—there is no such place for it.
Is there anyone who can speak it? After a long silence, he said, "Withdraw."
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: A lotus blooms upon dry land; the sea surges with Mount Ao. Who knows what night this is tonight?
Those in mountain forests and city markets alike come to behold it together. Raising his whisk, he says: "Look! Look!

The Buddha Sun-Moon-Lamp shines forth his original radiance from this very place. Through the six periods of day and night, there is no interruption whatsoever. He strikes the whisk once and says: "Blink!"
Having attained the eye, [he stands] behind the horse and before the donkey.
Ascending the hall: tumultuous and vast, silent and still. The ancient whip’s wind is high; the jade pitcher is bright at dawn. Looking to the left, there is no flaw.
Looking back, one has already grown old. Do you all understand? (He strikes the whisk. "The sound of wind and rain last night;
how many fallen flowers one knows.
At the Buddha’s Nirvana, over three hundred assemblies were entirely dead words; amidst the Śāla trees, they were turned into living ones.
Verse: Living within death, dying within life; The waters are green, the mountains are blue; Heaven is vast, the earth is wide.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Zhaozhou visiting Zhunyu. Zhaozhou took his staff and, in the Dharma Hall, walked from east to west and from west to east.
Zhunyu asked, "What are you doing? Zhaozhou said, "Probing the water. Zhunyu said, "In my place here, there is not even a single drop."
[The Master said: "Nothing. What is there to seek? Zhaozhou leaned his staff against [the wall] and went out. The Master said: "Although Zhunü was skilled at guarding the gate, what could he do?
The thief leaves with empty hands. Now tell me, what was Zhaozhou’s intention in leaning his staff against the wall and departing?
Xie Fajian ascends the hall: "Dull and dazed; simple and straightforward. Water and milk blend together, yet the liver and gall remain as far apart as Chu and Yue.
How can this be seen? Together we lean upon the balustrade, eyes wide with smiles, as the pines and cassias of the four mountains stir in the autumn wind."

Setting out for the Temple of King Aśoka, he took his leave of the assembly and ascended the hall. Fragmented and lingering, it punctuates the vast void; as it unfurls and rolls up, there is no place to find its tracks.
Driven by the winds of karma, it intentionally rolls along, then once more passes from the dragon over to another peak.
Record of the Sayings at Guangli Chan Temple on Mount Ayuwang in Qingyuan Prefecture,
compiled and edited by the disciples De Pu and others.
On the tenth day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of the Jingding era, the Master entered the temple.
He pointed to the three gates. "To intend is already to err; to move is already to be separated. He had already shifted the pivot of the lock.
Looking left and right, he said, "Is there anyone who enters and exits together? He let out a shout.
The Abbot held up his staff and said, "Here there is no place for you to enter or act.

The two patriarchs, Daie and Fozhao, exhausted all their skillful means, yet you all simply keep staring with wide-open eyes. With the staff, he drew a line and said, "Skulls are scattered across the wilds."
The Imperial Edict: The brilliant sun shines in the heavens; the pure wind sweeps across the earth. It opens and closes the myriad mechanisms of existence, stirring and inspiring all living beings.
Yet, as for the subtle message within it, how can it be proclaimed? Deyu said to the Venerable Vinaya Master: "Yellow is the paper; black is the character."
The Dharma Seat: borrowing function to clarify position, and borrowing position to clarify function. In this regard, the ancients have suffered many defeats.
At Mount Mao, the tongue cannot catch up with the galloping horse; using one wedge to extract another wedge.
Ascending the seat, he held up the incense and said: "This one offering of incense is respectfully offered to extend the longevity of the present Emperor.
May His Majesty live ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years!

We pray that the eighty-four thousand yojanas of Mount Sumeru shall be as the lofty majesty of Your Majesty’s lifespan, and that the thirteen layers of the Flower Treasury World shall encompass [the realm]."
Regarding the imperial domain of the sovereign’s enterprise, he next held up the incense and said:

"This one portion of incense is offered on behalf of the Grand Tutor, Grand Chancellor, Director of the Chancellery, and Duke of the State, along with all the civil and military officials of the court, to augment their years of service and longevity. Again, he held up the incense and said:
"This incense possesses nothing particularly marvelous, yet it is not commonplace; it is offered in worship to the former abbot of Jingci Temple in Lin’an Prefecture."
At Kuangxiao Chan Temple, the late Master Beijian Daoheshang, in order to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk, adjusted his robes, took his seat, and said:
"If you realize it before words, you remain stuck in the shell and lost in the seal; if you master it through speech, you are like one who fixes the pegs while playing the se.
Departing from these two paths, how do you meet [the Buddha]? A monk came forward and asked: "A single imperial edict issues forth from within the Forbidden Palace."
Urged on, Cifeng resided at Maofeng; today he opens the hall to proclaim the wondrous Dharma. Auspicious clouds and auspicious vapors shroud the void.
At this very moment, we pray to hear the essentials of the Dharma. The Master said: "A Black Iron Kunlun beneath a Golden Incense Burner. [The student] stepped forward and asked:

After the ritual for the Emperor’s longevity had concluded, [the student] asked, "I have already received the Master's instruction; as for the matter of the supreme vehicle of the ancestral lineage, what is it? The Master said, "The rooster knows the dawn is near;

the crane knows the midnight hour. [The student] further asked, "In the past, when King Min invited Luoshan to ascend the hall, Luoshan took the seat, gathered his *saṃghāṭī* robe with his hands, looked around to left and right, and then descended from the seat. What was the meaning of this? The Master said, "An iron banner."
Tiegu asked: "When Min Wang took Luoshan by the hand and said, 'How is this assembly on Vulture Peak any different from today?
What do you say to that? The Master said: "Spring wind spreads thorns everywhere. Tiegu asked: "Luoshan said, 'I thought Your Majesty was but a worldly man. What does that mean? The Master said:
"If you receive a punch, there must be a time for returning the punch. Tiegu asked: "As for Zen itself..."

The Master said, "Today the hall is opened and the fourfold assembly has gathered before the dais; what instruction do you have? The Master replied, "In the high waves of the third surge, the fish transforms into a dragon;
yet the deluded person still scoops water from the night pond. He then said, "Before Mount Zhengjue, clouds arise from a mere span."
Beyond Shaolin, mirages surge like waves. From this point on, the lineages branched out and the schools divided, circling a thousand times and a hundred turns;
here they were added, there they were subtracted—present in the South but absent in the North. To look upon it, it is as if one’s hand covers the bends of the Yellow River.
Now, how can the newly installed Yungwang manifest his power? Having no other recourse, he overturns everything at once.
Furthermore, let each person take it to heart and feel shame. There is no need for the gold that stops a child’s crying, nor the sword that settles a nation’s turmoil.
With songs of praise and bellies full, may we all rejoice in this era of peace and prosperity. Ultimately, what serves as the proof? The verdant cypress before Old Zhao’s courtyard;
it resembles the pine upon the stones of the Southern Mountains.
Again, it is cited: A monk asked the Sixth Patriarch, "Who can attain the essential meaning of Huangmei? The Patriarch said, "One who understands the Buddha-Dharma attains it.
The monk said, "Does the Master attain it? The Patriarch said, "I do not attain it. The monk said, "Why does the Master not attain it?
The Patriarch said, "I do not understand the Buddha-Dharma. The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "Clarified butter and poison; overturning rain and turning clouds. Unfinished.
This is beyond the ordinary. Do you all wish to see the Great Master Huineng? Poverty is the mediator to wealth.
That evening, during the informal discourse (*xiaochan*), there was no place for entry. When the light sail catches a favorable wind, the path is immediately opened. A beggar sees a small profit;
thus, in this way, there is an inch-long and a foot-short, and not in that way, there is a foot-short and an inch-long. Now, turn it around!
The critical phrase (*huatou*). Furthermore, how can one chew and swallow it? Six extraordinary excellences and eight auspicious signs; thorns covering the ground, briars piercing the heavens.
Deshan and Linji have worn their teeth through to their gums; Yunmen and Zhaozhou have clenched their fists until their nails pierce through.
Each reveals the other, yet none knows the other. Tonight, at Yuyang, I shall borrow another path to meet you all.
He departs. He takes up his staff, strikes it once, and says: "In shallow water there are no fish; to cast down the hook in vain is useless.
Again, he cites Deshan’s address to the assembly: "Tonight, for this small session of inquiry, I shall not answer questions. Anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows of the staff.
At that time, a monk stepped forward, and Deshan struck him immediately. The monk said, "I have not even asked a question; why do you strike me? Deshan replied, "Because you have already spoken."
Shan said, "Where are you from? The monk replied, "I am a man from Silla. Shan said, "Before you have even stepped onto the ship’s railing, thirty blows of the staff would be well-deserved for you.
The Master said, "De-shan spreads a net that covers the heavens; this monk leaps through the Dragon Gate in secret.
Nevertheless, though it is so, he gains nothing to compensate for his labor."
[The Master] ascends the hall for the two orders of monks. Holding up his staff, he says: "Seven hands and eight feet; three heads and two faces.
Where there is a place to gather it in, there is no place to unfurl it. At times he cuts off the vital ford; at times he rolls out or rolls up according to conditions.
When it is not like this at all—how then do you see me? He leans on the staff and says: "Do not touch it. If you touch it, then..."
It breaks your donkey’s back.
Entering the city to visit the monastery, he ascends the hall and says: “Dark tiles hold frost that chills the traveler’s dream; Bright windows let in sunlight, lending morning warmth.
Unable to keep my mouth shut, I sit by the hearth; With robes tucked in, I vainly hasten to the gate of painted halberds. How pitiable, how laughable!”
Dongzhu: "Watching the monkey performance at Tianjin Bridge—whom can I discuss this meaning with? The elder’s son has no trousers.
He ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said: "For those who enter through the gate of Samantabhadra, even walls, tiles, and rubble shall trigger your awakening."

For those who enter through the gate of Avalokiteśvara, the frog and the earthworm serve as the catalyst for you. But tell me: for those who enter through empty space, whom would you have act as the catalyst?
He strikes the meditation staff once and says: "A crane flies through a thousand fathoms of snow; a dragon rises from a single pool of ice."
When Acharya Dengci ascended the hall, he held up his staff and said: "To act while there is no acting—dragons gallop and phoenixes soar.
To act while there is no acting—thunder is hidden and lightning is withdrawn. A single drop of water possesses the power to swell the vast ocean;
with lethal poison, one practices the compassion of equality. This is still merely the ordinary usage. When we meet today, how will it be? (He leaned the staff against the wall.)
He said: "Letting one move pass by; master and guest complete.
Upon receiving the news of the passing of Master Huaihai of Jingshan, he ascended the hall and said: "The clouds over Huai are bleak and dim; the waters of Huai have run dry.
The Old Man of Jingshan has nothing to say. With a shout, the mountain cliffs shatter into a hundred pieces. In the end, his total presentation is most intimate."
Laughing without end, weeping without end—Kauṇḍinya was so startled that he stuck out his tongue.
Upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: many hairs form a ball, many waters form a stream, many people form a marketplace, and many clods of earth form a mound.
King Aśoka gathered the assembly for the summer retreat. What did he achieve? After a long silence, he said: "This summer in the eastern province;
next summer in the western province.
He ascended the hall and cited an instance where one day Danxia visited National Teacher Nanyang. It happened that the National Teacher was asleep, so Danxia asked the attendant...
The Master said, "Is the National Teacher here? The other replied, "He is indeed here; it is simply that he does not see you. Xiang said, "That is far too remote.
The other replied, "Not only do you, Venerable One, fail to see him; even Buddha-Eye could not look upon him. Xiang said, "A dragon gives birth to a dragon."
"A phoenix gives birth to a phoenix chick. He then went out. When the National Teacher woke from his sleep, the attendant recounted the previous conversation.
The National Teacher struck him with twenty blows and drove him out. Hearing this, Danxia said, "He truly does not fail as the National Teacher of Nanyang.
The Master said, "The attendant met the thief face-to-face. But tell me, where exactly was he caught by the thief? If you can understand this, [you will understand] the National Teacher."
To ensure that [the Dharma] does not circulate in vain.

He ascended the hall and raised this case: A monk asked Mazu, "Leaving behind the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations, I ask you, Master, to point directly to the meaning of the Westward Journey.
Mazu said, "I have a headache today; I cannot explain it for you. Go ask Zhizang. The monk then went to ask him.
Zang said, "I am weary today and cannot explain it for you. Go ask my elder brother Hai. The monk went to ask Hai, who said, "When I reach this point, I do not understand either.
The monk returned and reported this to Mazu, who said, "Zang’s head is white; Hai’s head is black.
The Master said, "The ocean may dry up, yet its bottom will eventually be seen; when a person dies, their mind is no longer known."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The oriole sings among the green willows; the butterflies dance amidst the fragrant clusters. The scenery urges one on—please, Master, lift us up.

The Master said, "Blind your eyes! The monk pressed further: "But what can be done? At the ridge, the cuckoo urges the plowing with urgency; beneath the flowers, the *tíhú* bird busies itself urging the drinking.
The Master said, "You have smashed your skull. The monk said, "I remember it. [This refers to] a monk asking Baizhang about "clutching the raw jade."
He approached the Master and requested that the Master provide a definitive resolution. The Master said, "Last night, a tiger on South Mountain bit a great beast.

What was the meaning of this? The Master replied, "The true does not conceal the false. [The student] pressed further, saying, "It is no mistake regarding the true exposition; why then do you not grant us a skillful means? The Master said:
"A man who covers his ears while stealing a bell. Furthermore, how is this so? The Master said, "Adding a cup after one is already drunk.
The student continued, "If there is no Zhonglang to examine it, it is the same as firewood in a wild shed. The Master then struck him. Tell me, where does this monk’s fault lie? The Master said:

He received one ox from a man and returned a horse to another. The monk bowed and said: "I went to Touzi three times and ascended to Dongshan nine times. Auspicious gold does not leap from the furnace;
ten thousand functions have ceased, and even the thousand sages carry nothing with them. Yet there is still the debt of buying straw sandals remaining.
This fellow carrying a wooden board sees only one side; he cannot pull back, nor can he push forward. The Persian has lost his way.
[The Master] holds up a document case and says: "Within the moon, Lady Heng-e laughs as she unveils the heavens.
He ascends the hall. He cites the story of Mazu ascending the hall: when the assembly had just gathered, Baizhang came forward and rolled up his sitting mat;

Mazu immediately descended from the seat and returned to the abbot’s quarters, where he asked Baizhang: "Just now I ascended the hall and did not speak a single word; for what reason did you [roll up your mat]?"
[Zhaozhou] rolled up his mat. Zhao said, "Yesterday, I was pinched by the Master until my nose ached. The Patriarch said, "Where did you apply your mind yesterday?
Zhao said, "Today my nose does not ache anymore. The Patriarch said, "You have deeply grasped the matter of today.
The Master [Dongshan] said: "A father is compassionate and a son is filial; the small are clever and the great are dull-witted. If one were to act according to the command,"
As soon as he saw the mat being rolled up, he immediately expelled him. Why? Because once one has passed through the Dragon Gate, the waves and winds become even more perilous.
On the occasion of the Longevity Festival, [the Master] ascended the hall: not deviating from his original vow, he manifested birth like that of Śākyamuni Buddha;

secretly deploying true compassion, his capacity was as vast as Māyādevī’s. As a mother figure to a single Sage and as a nurturer of the myriad realms, his dignity is peerless and his virtue difficult to fathom.
[The Master] ascends the hall on the occasion of the Qianhui Festival. "The Supreme Truth of the Holy Path (Paramārtha-satya) is such that its wisdom is unfathomable and its depth is immeasurable.

The Buddhas have expounded it without exhausting it, yet sentient beings follow it without knowing it. He suddenly grasps his staff and says: "O staff! [The assembly] offers their threefold benediction;

the monks in the forest point to Mount Sumeru as incense for his long life. *Note: This passage is from the recorded sayings of a Chan master. The "threefold benediction" refers to the traditional Chinese ritual of offering blessings for longevity. The staff (*zhuzhang*) is a symbol of the master’s authority and the lineage of transmission.*

For a long time this essential point has been kept silent; I have not sought to speak of it hastily. [He strikes once with his staff. On the ninth day of the fourth month, the Qianhui Festival, the summer retreat begins.
In the midst of the red dust and purple lanes lies the monastery of Perfect Enlightenment. Plowing the neighbor’s field and seizing the ox—this is the Wisdom of Equality.
Gold cannot be bartered for gold; water cannot wash away water. For what reason did Deshan set up his signboard in the marketplace?

He ascended the hall [to give a sermon] (expressing thanks for presiding over the whisk and managing the meal). It is said in the teachings: "That which is equal regarding food is also equal regarding the Dharma.

If this is truly so, then when the head monk of the administrative office prepares the meal and the head seat presides over the whisk, the donor and the recipient, the speaker and the listener, are all equal and without distinction.

There is a difference. Food consists of form, fragrance, flavor, touch, and mental objects (*dharmas*). Apart from seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, how can you explain the principle of "equality"?
[The Master] strikes the whisk and says: "The former sings 'yu'; the latter sings 'yong'."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: Layman Pang asked Mazu, "The person who is fundamentally unobscured—please, Master, cast your eyes high.
Mazu looked straight down. The Layman said, "This is a single stringless lute; only you, Master, can play it wondrously.
Mazu looked straight up. The Layman bowed. Mazu then returned to his quarters. The Layman followed him in and said, "Seeking cleverness, one ends up clumsy. The Master said, "The higher..."
I lower that which is high and raise that which is low. Shoulders pressed together yet walking out of step; hands joined yet worlds apart like clouds and mud. Entering the hall:
The Sage has no self, yet there is nowhere he does not manifest as self. A tiger bites a great tiger; a snake swallows a turtle’s nose.
This old monk speaks these words of truth to people, waiting only for empty space to fall to the ground.

Ascending the hall to pray for rain: there is a single phrase that reaches you—it is like a mirage quenching thirst. There is not a single phrase that reaches you—it is like water emerging from high ground.
Look at it and you see four corners and six sides; stir it and you find seven hollows and eight protrusions.

One who is skilled at observing the winds and clouds and discerning the seasonal shifts will say: "When meeting the day-stem *geng*, there is change. Yet, matters do not always follow a single direction. (He strikes the whisk.)
The Bodhisattva Dragon King travels through the rain to moisten all;

he obstructs his body with layers of clouds rising upward. Upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: ten thousand *li* without a blade of grass; the heels of one's feet do not touch the ground. Once you step out the door, it is all grass again.
Riding a crane to Yangzhou—dare I ask you all, how do you conduct yourselves? (He strikes the whisk and says: "Transforming iron into gold."
It is easy to change metal and stone; it is difficult to exhort others to eliminate right and wrong.
Entering the hall, he raised the example of Layman Pang, who one day fell in the snow. His daughter, Lingzhao, went and lay down beside him.
The Layman said, "What are you doing? Zhao said, "I see my father fallen to the ground; I have come specifically to help him up. The Layman then rose and departed.
The Master said, "A great villain is easily broken, but a domestic thief is difficult to guard against."

Ascending the hall: Never having been in close proximity, one is already separated by a great thousandfold world-system. When the wind blows upon the fire, as soon as there is something valued, it immediately becomes a stagnant pitfall.
Like a boat drifting with the current, Zhaozhou makes use of the twelve hours, while Yongming turns every day into one hundred and eight matters.
"In Guoqing, the talented are noble; in this household, the children are pampered. O people of Mount Mao, I dare ask you:
what is your current pursuit? (He strikes the whisk. Unless one knows how to ride a donkey backward by oneself, one will spend a lifetime following after others.
Ascending the hall: The frosty wind has not yet faded; the cherished scenery is like spring. The void is utterly traceless, filling every atom of the universe.
Today and tomorrow, one flits with joy and flits with anger, secretly selling one’s elegance to others.
On the Double Ninth, the Master ascended the hall. He cited Elder Zhenneng’s instruction to the assembly: "On the ninth day there is no white wine; one eats heartily of yellow chestnut cakes.
On the tenth day there are yellow chrysanthemums; they urge us to thresh the grain. Before the five-o'clock bell has even rung, the neighbor's rooster has already crowed several times.
When we meet on the road, we do not dismount from our horses; each hurries toward their own destination. The Master said: "Elder Zhenneng valued his purchase."
To sell [the wine] cheaply—Mount Mao does not do so. On the ninth day there is no white ale; purple *yū* flowers are brewed with tea.
When discussing "Ascending High" through the ages, who has trodden the path of the Ancient Sovereign? Fallen leaves stir the true wind; yellow chrysanthemums speak of the profound essentials.
I laugh at myself for being so senseless, as we are led together into the wild weeds.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] cited the story of Baizhang’s second visit to Mazu. While standing in attendance, Mazu looked with his eyes toward the whisk in the corner of the meditation seat.
Baizhang said, "Use this very thing; do not depart from the use of this. Mazu asked, "After you have opened your two flaps of skin [to preach], how will you act for others?
Baizhang picked up the whisk and held it upright. Mazu said, "Use this very thing; do not depart from the use of this. Baizhang hung the whisk back on its stand.
At the old site, the Patriarch let out a thunderous shout, which left Baizhang deaf for three days straight. The Master said:
"A lute player cannot shift his temperament unless he enters the vast ocean; a kunpeng bird cannot transform its form unless it rides the whirlwind.
Thus, regarding the path that points upward, even 'cracking' and 'pecking' are still at odds. Do you all wish to understand why Baizhang was deaf for three days?"
A dragon-spring sword tempered a hundred times leaps into the great abyss.
Entering the hall: spring rain is like rich fat; spring clouds are like cranes; spring grasses grow lushly; spring flowers blaze forth.
To ride upon sound and cover over form—how excessively extravagant! Not a hair’s breadth of form appears, yet it fills the ditches and blocks the valleys. It goes straight ahead without obstruction.
Yet there remains one move lacking.

On the occasion of the Emperor’s Longevity Festival, he ascends the hall: With profound compassion and vast vows, you nurture the sagely brilliance; Your majesty stands foremost as the model for the myriad nations.
The merit of your long life is beyond naming; The color of Mount Sumeru is ever more green.

Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Qian Hexagram festival, [the Master] said: "The great governing principle of the fundamental source is the pearl within the topknot of the Wheel-Turning King.
It cannot be grasped by the hand; it cannot be reached by the mind. Precisely at this moment of the 'Ninth Yang' of Qian, he suddenly picks up his staff and says:
'O staff! Here, you go forth with your heart laid bare, piece by piece. He strikes the ground once with the staff and says: 'Wondrous Virtue honors the universe; lofty brilliance lifts the heavens.'"
The Great Void.

Opening the Summer Retreat, he ascends the hall: "Restraining the feet to protect life binds the hound of Han and demands its catch; fixing a date for realization shackles the qí-jì steed and forces it to gallop.
If one is thus lost, like a wind blowing against the sun or carrying Mount Sumeru on one's back—how then shall it be? Nü.
The mountain peaks are a vast net that covers the heavens;
you must penetrate it. [He] ascended the hall and raised the following case: When Prefect Li Ao asked a monk, "What words and phrases did Mazu have?
the monk replied, "He said 'this mind is Buddha,' and he also said 'neither mind nor Buddha. The Prefect said, "Put both aside for a moment. The Prefect then asked [another monk about] Xuefeng...
Master Zang was in the hall. Zang called out, "Prefect! Prefect! The Prefect responded, "Yes. Zang said, "The drums and horns are sounding.
The Master said, "The *kui* pities the millipede; the millipede pities the snake. All have been seen through by this monk in secret."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Chan Master Dazhu Huizhu. A lecturer came to visit him and asked, "Lecturer, what sutra do you lecture on?
The lecturer replied, "The Samādhi Sutra. Huizhu held up his staff and said, "What samādhi is this? The lecturer was at a loss. Huizhu said, "I am an old monk;
my affairs as abbot are many and busy, so I cannot beat you. The Master said, "At that time, upon seeing..."
He raised his staff and said, "What samādhi is this? To which he replied, "I have already presented it to the Master.
Later, while ascending the hall during the summer retreat, he held up his staff and said, "In the first forty-five days that have passed, crimson clouds pierce the azure void."
Forty-five days have not yet passed; the sun circles Mount Sumeru precisely on this very day. Above, there is no scheme to pierce the heavens;
below, there is no plot to enter the earth. He strikes the table once and says: "The General’s arrow struck the tiger of the South Mountain;
it was originally but an old stone from Lantian."

Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “Two dragons contend for a pearl; who is the one that gets it? Zhaozhou said, “I, this old monk, simply watch. The Master said:
“This monk’s posing of this question is much like a retired prime minister recounting the story of his youth when he passed the imperial examinations before the very eyes of those in office.
It is exactly the same. But as for Zhaozhou saying, ‘I, this old monk, simply watch’—what does that mean? Although...”
The supreme horse-power still possesses a mind that kills people.
Entering the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Take one step where there is no place to go; a sweet melon is sweet all the way to its stem.
Speak one word where there is nothing to say; a bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip. Sweeping away all the idle Buddhas and patriarchs of the past, to trigger the mechanism..."
"This is a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt. He threw down his staff and descended from the seat.

On the day after the Buddha’s enlightenment, he ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said: "O Great Assembly! For six years on the Snowy Mountains, that old fellow with the yellow face endured freezing cold and hunger.
What did he think he would achieve? It turns out he simply could not tolerate having sand in his eyes. Then he struck [the assembly].
Thus he points to emptiness and speaks of emptiness; he grasps at emptiness and blocks off emptiness. Holding up his staff, he says: "For ten thousand ages it remains in disarray;
the rain-soaked plum blossoms open in the damp morning breeze."
The True Master of the Ultimate Truth ascends the hall: "The Vinaya is not bondage; Chan is not liberation. The butterfly dreams of Zhuang Zhou; Duke Zhou establishes rites and music.
If you realize this, all things are of one family; if you do not realize it, there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences.
Do you understand? A single sheet of white cloud rises upon the ridge; several times it parts, yet again it covers."
Ascending the hall: The spring colors are harmonious and radiant; the fragrance of flowers is dense and pervasive. All six windows are unlocked, leaving no trace where they once were.

Leaning together upon the precarious railing, one’s body stands within a world of profound stillness. Almost ready to bring forth the whole teaching, it first leaks away—slippery lips as the yellow bird plays in the spring breeze.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "All dharmas, from their very origin, have always been characterized by quiescent extinction. The jade hare sinks in the west;
the golden crow rises in the east—going thus, you would sit the *śrāmaṇera* to death; not going thus, you would run the *upādhyāya* to death. He took up his staff, drew a line, and said:
"A stone ox blocks the ancient road; one horse gives birth to three tigers."
The Buddha ascends the hall for the Nirvana assembly. Stirring up dust and raising clouds of soil; the adamantine true body is sevenfold topsy-turvy and eightfold inverted.
At the gate of great tranquil concentration, he strikes his whisk and says: "Misty peaks stretching across the void add a hue of sorrow; forest trees and rain-soaked flowers bear traces of tears."
When the Elder Faxi arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "The one path that points upward—there, even 'cracking' and 'pecking' are still at odds.

When water and milk blend together, the liver and gallbladder become as distant as Chu and Yue. When Nanyue asked Mazu, 'What is it? and when Baling presented Yunmen’s three turns of speech—what was their intent?
A child born posthumously has no form in the heart."
Ascending the hall, he said: "At the moment of seeing the seeing, rain washes the tender petals of the pale-red peach blossoms;
that which sees is not the seeing, as the wind shakes the light-green willow filaments. Even seeing is already detached from seeing—strange rocks are revealed amidst the shadows of white clouds.
Seeing cannot reach it—the ancient trees are clear within the radiance of flowing water. Is there anyone here who knows the time and recognizes the season? He let out a shout.
On the anniversary of the passing of Master Beijian, he held up the incense and said: "The original edition is stubborn and headstrong; it cannot be lifted even by a spoon.
It tethers the clouds to their stalks and patches empty space; on dry land, the heavens overflow with white waves. In the dark, he draws forth the staff of fixed destiny;
even hawk-eyes and falcon-spirits are bewildered as to its direction. Old Monk, for whose sake do you gnash your teeth until your death? Let him be allowed to leave the world in doubt."
Six days before his passing, Layman Xuji ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he struck it once and said: "If you seek the ox, you must see its tracks.
In the places where you all eat porridge and rice, and in the places where you turn, move, bow, and look up—do you see the tracks? When the tracks are there, is the ox also there?"
"Do you see the ox? Even if it were standing out in the open, one could not drive it away. When the practice is matured, its pure whiteness is rare and extraordinary.
Who is it that lets go or holds fast? "Moo-hoo, moo-hoo! [The Master] throws down his staff and says:
"When neither person nor ox is seen, this is precisely the time of the bright moon."
Small Assembly for the Summer Retreat: From the Western Heaven to this land, how many heroic spirits have been obstructed by a single idle public case from two thousand years ago?
They are utterly unable to make even a single movement. Their eyes grow three-cornered; their heads stand as steep as the Five Peaks. Arrow—!
When the string is taut, one cannot help but shoot. To enter this fortress and break this fortress within the monastery of Perfect Enlightenment (Yuanjue), one must employ the Wisdom of Equality.
Whether a donkey’s ears are long or a horse’s ears are short, with four corners planted firmly on the ground, flies will swarm to the stinking meat—who else could care?

At Bowel-Basin Peak, clouds gather and clouds disperse; in East Qian Lake, the water is deep and the water is shallow. When the mountain monk makes such an announcement, do not— (Do not misunderstand.)

"Is there anyone who can shake their head sideways? He suddenly seized his staff, struck it once on the ground, and said: "The vanguard has made its move; the rearguard has no merit. He then cited an old case:
When Yangshan was at Mount Mushi, he was tending cattle on a slope. He saw a monk climbing the mountain, who came up and went down again before long.
Yangshan asked him, "Why do you not stay? Is there some circumstance that does not accord with you? The monk—
Yangshan said, "The Master asked me, 'What is your name? I replied, 'Returning to Reality. The Master asked, 'Where does Reality return?
I could not answer. Yangshan said, 'Go back again. If the Master asks you, "Where does Reality return? simply say:"
"Within the eyes, within the ears, within the nose"—this monk acted exactly as he was instructed. Deshan said, "A man of empty words and deception;
these were the words of a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) to five hundred people. The Master said, "He flaunts his brilliance in the light and practices deception in the dark.
If it had been this monk, he would have galloped with his horse's hooves swift in the spring breeze, seeing all the flowers of Chang’an in a single day."
When the summer retreat ends, one cannot even swallow or chew; it is always manifest before one. If one attempts to preserve it as a whole, it instead breaks into two pieces.

Those who act the moment they are touched strike their heads and bump their foreheads, dying on level ground. When all eight directions are transparently clear, a single thought lasts ten thousand years.
Ten thousand years in a single thought—what more need be said of the "binding" on the fifteenth day of the fourth month? A frog at the bottom of the well swallows the moon.
The "unbinding" on the fifteenth day of the seventh month: Louzhi’s fist is as large as a bowl; he coldly laughs at the old, ancient Chan master of Shaoyang.
A sharp blade that cuts away what people cherish—even granted such a thing, you all, can you still avoid paying the price for the meal?
Striking the whisk, he said: "The lotus petals fall red, veiling the jade mirror; the well-locus leaves turn azure, dotting the silver bed."
Again, the case is raised. A monk asked Caoshan, "In such heat, where can one seek refuge? Caoshan said, "Seek refuge within the boiling cauldrons and the glowing furnaces.
The monk said, "But how does one seek refuge within the boiling cauldrons and the glowing furnaces?
Caoshan said, "The various sufferings cannot reach there. The Master said: "Amidst thorns and blades, within the silken music of the inner chambers—why need the majestic phoenix [seek elsewhere]?"
Dwelling among the green paulownias, the Dragon Reclining [in the depths] will never reflect in still water.
During the summer retreat, the Tathāgata has esoteric words: gold is born from the beautiful waters, and Kāśyapa did not conceal it; jade emerges from Mount Kunlun.
To face it, a giant serpent coils around one's feet; to turn away from it, a colorful phoenix soars to the heavens.
Neither facing nor turning away, dust is raised and earth is scattered—earth vast and sky wide. Whether for a long term or a short term, all are merely following a map to seek a horse.
When Ci-feng reached this point, he could do nothing but scoop salt into his hand. With urgent business at home, he struck the whisk and said: "Many laugh at me; they mock me."
When Daci was sweeping the ground, Zhaozhou asked, "What is the essence of Prajñā?
Daci replied, "What is the essence of Prajñā? Zhaozhou laughed heartily.
The next day, while Zhaozhou was sweeping the ground, Daci asked, "What is the essence of Prajñā? Zhaozhou set down his broom and laughed heartily.
He then returned to his quarters. The Master said, "Daci is artful but not upright; Zhaozhou is upright but not artful.
As for the essence of Prajñā, neither has even dreamed of it."
The Summer Retreat concludes. For one hundred and twenty days, every day is a good day. From India to China, countless heroic spirits have equally followed the Buddha’s command;
within that interval, each has practiced according to their own way and each has attained realization according to their own experience.
Yet among those under my jurisdiction in Mingzhou, within Mount Ciyun, the Zen practitioners—each and every one of them—with nostrils reaching toward the heavens and eyes...

Not hanging on the door, the mind does not dwell in the profound mystery. Inhaling the lake’s radiance, chewing the mountain’s emerald green, emerging in seven ways and disappearing in eight, tumbling eastward and crashing westward—rolling all the way to this day, it is nonetheless free and joyful. Even this mountain monk can do nothing about it.

Nevertheless, as the saying goes: "The sweet melon is sweet to the very stem; the bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip. Again, he raised the case where Qianfeng addressed the assembly, saying: "Lift up!"
"One cannot raise two; to let one pass is to fall into the second. Yunmen came forward from the assembly and said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan.
Feng said, "Tomorrow there shall be no communal labor. The Master said, "Some might say:
'Rising early at the fifth watch, there are still travelers on the night road. This is so, yet as for Qian..."
Fengdao said: "Tomorrow there will be no communal labor (fǔqǐng). Furthermore, what then? "A great achievement is not rewarded. Winter Solstice.

The clothes are worn through, the elbows are exposed; the fire is cold, the clouds are deep. To depart in this manner would be a grievous waste of people. Letting out a single thread, there is another way to manifest transformation.
